Economics is not the purpose of society, it is a byproduct of it. Nobody can produce everything they need to sustain themselves, so goods will need to be exchanged. There will always need to be a system for determining the relative value of two unrelated goods. Economics is the term for this category of systems.

Bartering is still an economy. I grow apples, you grow oranges, I trade you a bushel of apples for your bushel of oranges. Another man down the road raises horses. How many apples is it for him to give me a horse? How many apples a week to rent one? How many apples for him to train a horse that I bring him? This is why we abstract bartering to currency. The first currency was gold, valued by weight, because that was valuable to everyone. Later, we decided it was easier to let someone else hold onto the gold, and we'd just hand them a note that was signed by the gold-holder saying it was redeemable for gold. Nowadays we still have the notes, but you can't redeem them anywhere.

You can still barter with currency. You can make money by trading one currency for another when exchange rates are favorable and watching the market while diversifying your holdings between different currencies, and continuously trade up. It is possible to make a living exclusively by doing this. Anyone who is rich and has half a brain is already doing this to a degree, because if you have $10,000,000 all in USD, you're only a multi-millionaire as long as the dollar is strong. The moment the dollar is weak, you become poorer. So instead you have some of your money in USD, some in euro, some in yuan, some in yen, some in gold, etc.

Hell, governments do that exact thing (image is global distribution of reserve currencies). The US Dollar's primary value stems from the fact that petroleum is traded under USD, so the US Dollar is valuable as a reserve currency because it's effectively backed by petroleum instead of gold (when you hear the term "petrodollar", this is what they're talking about). Most US currency is held by foreign governments as a reserve currency so that their government can still operate even if its own currency collapses.

You will never not have economics. You can just abstract it sufficiently that it's difficult for most people to understand, which is precisely what we have done. This is why people are convinced that money is a thing, rather than a means of getting things.
